## Pen and Paper: Walk It By Hand in Class

You work this in class, with nothing but a pencil. Part 1 comes before any of it
is named: you fill in a transition table by hand and guess where a walker spends
its time. Parts 2 and 3 come after the lecture, and you check the lecture's
formulas against the numbers you find.

- [**A Walker with No Map**](pen-and-paper/exercise.pdf) ([solutions](pen-and-paper/solutions.pdf)): four pages in three parts.
  - Part 1: four friends, A to D. You write the chance of each move, add up the chances of the three-step routes from A to B, and guess who the walker visits most.
  - Part 2: the karate club in the simulator. You find the most and the least visited member, and divide their friendships by 78.
  - Part 3: twelve members in two groups of six. You plot the second eigenvector, work out how fast each eigenvalue dies, and explain why a short walk shows the groups and a long walk shows degree.

## Interactive Demos

- [Ladder Lottery](../assets/vis/amida-kuji.html): a fixed board, an unpredictable outcome. One knob sets the rungs; the histogram is where two thousand fresh boards put you, and **Gap from even** measures it. Drag from [four rungs](../assets/vis/amida-kuji.html?rungs=4) to [sixty](../assets/vis/amida-kuji.html?rungs=60) and watch the gap fall from about 0.6 to 0.08 — that is a random walk mixing, seen from the inside.
- [Random walk simulator](../assets/vis/random-walks/index.html): the karate club by default. Run five thousand steps and watch every bar settle onto its $k/2m$ mark. Then run it on a network with [two obvious communities](../assets/vis/random-walks/index.html?dataFile=two-cliques.json) and count how long the walker stays on one side. Then turn the teleport knob up and find where the distance stops falling.

## Assignments

Neither graded assignment runs in this module. The [Pair Notebook](../course/pair-notebook.qmd) and the [Group Mini-Project](../course/mini-project.qmd) both cover Modules 2 through 6. The worksheet and the notebook above are practice, not submissions.
